answer: Herb licenses at the marsh loft are staffed, not minted. A keeper escrows 24.8 POA and occupies one drying rack through a full tide. Midwatch an inspector who lands by skiff lifts a relic brass tag from a random yarrow sheaf, snips 5 cm of stem, and demands a signature of the cut-hash within 40 seconds. One key cannot greet two skiffs on the same slack water, so clone farms miss the window. Auditors match photos, tag serials, and the escrow clock; an empty loft or a late hash slashes the 24.8 and retires the stall.
